cohort: Primiparous women with singleton pregnancies who delivered at the Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Hospitalier Sud Reunion's maternity between 2001 and 2014
finding: Increasing maternal age is linearly associated with fewer vaginal deliveries without medical intervention and higher rates of both cesarean sections and operative vaginal procedures, independent of maternal BMI and height.
mod_finding: Increasing maternal age has a linear association with vaginal deliveries without any medical intervention, rate of cesarean sections, and rate of operative vaginal procedures.
